clue.text: National topic of conversation

definitions.meaning: a national of a country is a citizen, one owing allegiance to its crown or state
the matter being discussed or talked about

explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a monarchy is a subject of the crown, and the theme of a discussion is its subject too.

clue.text: Most stylish things for babies to wear, in a way

indicators.note: the baby garments are set inside the abbreviation for a way, so 'in' signals containment

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
nappies are the British word for diapers

explanation.surface: Fashion notes on the smartest baby clothes, in some manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as a hedge, but 'in' is the container signal and 'a way' is a street. Nappies are what Americans call diapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy is informal for smart or stylish, so the superlative means most stylish.

clue.text: Handsome chap on screen, so they say

definitions.text: Handsome chap on screen, so they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the spoken words stand for a written name

parts.note: a beau is a handsome young man, placed on guard, a word for screen as in shield

explanation.surface: Gossip about a good-looking film star.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAU GUARD said aloud gives the surname of Dirk Bogarde, the British matinee idol, so the whole clue is also his description.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirk Bogarde was a famously good-looking British film actor, a heart-throb of 1950s cinema.

clue.text: Tenant with no right initially to go in

indicators.note: the tenant's word is left lacking a letter, so 'with no' signals removal

parts.note: a renter is someone who pays rent, a tenant

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word right

explanation.surface: A lodger without the right to go inside first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes from RENTER the R that 'right initially' supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go into it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Sweet kid the girl shut out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child shuts the girl out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'shut out', but it is the anagram signal for KID THE GIRL SHUT, fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkish delight is a confection of gel dusted with sugar, a classic sweet.

clue.text: Pop celeb introduced as a cad

indicators.note: the celebrity is brought into the word for father, so 'introduced' signals insertion

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A famous singer is unveiled as a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests pop music, but here it is the informal word for father, and 'introduced' sets the celebrity inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A dastard is an old word for a contemptible coward, the same kind of person as a cad.

clue.text: See 4
Film director's line with classical composer

parts.note: a line is a glib sales pitch, a spiel
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A movie-maker's patter set alongside music by a great composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Spielberg directed Jaws and E.T., among many films.

clue.text: Increase intended to be announced at end of month

indicators.note: the sound piece is placed after the short month, so this phrase orders the two parts

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

indicators.note: announcing is saying aloud, so the word for intended is taken by its sound

parts.note: meant is a synonym of intended

explanation.surface: A rise planned to be declared when the month closes, like a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to make something larger, a synonym of increase as a verb.

clue.text: Dainty woman, say, with no children

definitions.meaning: small and neat, as in British slang for something cute and petite
a person with dual income and no kids yet, here a childless woman given as an example

explanation.definitionFit: Dinky is British for neat and dainty; the acronym for dual income, no kids yet makes it a childless earner.

clue.text: Language a learner finally understood

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word learner

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, so got means understood

explanation.surface: A student at last grasped the foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a particular group, a kind of language.

clue.text: Arriving drunk, I note

parts.note: rolling, as in rolling drunk, describes someone very drunk

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a person turned up intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll in is to turn up casually or late, so it means arriving.

clue.text: Exhibition venue left largely in a mess: artist has it fixed

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA means Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of largely are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gallery left untidy, but the painter has repaired it.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist with 'it' attached sits after 'left' in the answer, before the jumbled 'largely'; 'has' and 'fixed' only join them.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait gallery is a museum showing pictures of people, a place for exhibitions.

clue.text: English trees rot

parts.note: a yew is an evergreen tree
an ash is a deciduous tree

explanation.surface: English woodland is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: One plural 'trees' gives two trees in turn, YEW and ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or humbug, which is what rot means as slang.

clue.text: Sue and Amanda playing around to a tiresome degree

indicators.note: messing about here means the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two women fooling around until everyone is bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; only SUE and AMANDA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means until sickness, said of something repeated to the point of boredom.

clue.text: Here lecturer works and plays

parts.note: a place where an academic gives talks to students, and also where dramas are staged

explanation.definitionFit: A university hall where academics give talks shares its name with the playhouse where dramas are staged.

clue.text: Aim of surgeon principally — to follow medical procedure

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
O is an abbreviated of, as in o'clock

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, picking out the leading letter of surgeon

parts.note: to copy is to follow someone's example

explanation.surface: The surgeon's main goal is to carry out the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Endoscopy is an examination of the inside of the body with a camera tube, a hospital procedure.

clue.text: Film Tati shot near French resort getting cut

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the director's name is rearranged
the resort's name is shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Jacques Tati filming on the Riviera has his footage edited.
explanation.walkthrough: Tati is the French film director; 'shot' looks like filming but rearranges TATI into TITA, and 'getting cut' takes E from NICE to leave NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic is James Cameron's 1997 film about the sinking liner.

clue.text: Heard Bangkok Shipping Company established link

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a shipping company from Bangkok would be a Thai line, line being a shipping firm

explanation.surface: Word is that an Asian shipping firm has set up a connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie line is a fixed telephone connection between two exchanges, a set communication route.

clue.text: London book store?

parts.note: London is the capital of Britain
to book a seat is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A London bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a pun: a capital reserve is a store of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital reserve is money held back by a company, a stock or store of wealth.

clue.text: Made good time in outfit he had put together

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time is set inside the other pieces, so 'in' signals containment

parts.note: he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: Someone corrected their timing while assembling a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put together' joins the outfit and the contraction; 'in' drops the time letter between their halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to make it good, so righted means made good.

clue.text: See 18
Fancy non-drinker inhaling joint

indicators.note: breathing in takes the joint inside the teetotaller

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker
a hough is the hock joint of an animal's leg

explanation.surface: A teetotaller smoking cannabis is an amusing idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette, but it is HOUGH, the hock or ankle joint of a hind leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or idea, as is a thought.

clue.text: Assumptions about attitudes to drink after opening of pub

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its leading letter, here of pub

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to sup is to drink
positions are attitudes or stances

explanation.surface: Notions about how people feel about drinking, at the start of pub opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' says the rest follows the first letter of 'pub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presuppositions are things taken for granted beforehand, which is what assumptions are.

clue.text: Religious group's guide

parts.note: pi is informal British slang for pious or religious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A guidebook for a church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides ships into harbour, so a pilot is a guide.

clue.text: Expression of joy from Central America

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A cry of happiness from a country in the isthmus.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a cheerful exclamation sung or said when happy.

clue.text: Cheese I select for grating — ends of stale Cheddar

indicators.note: grating cheese breaks it up, so the letters are rearranged
the ends of the two words here are their closing letters

explanation.surface: Picking a cheese to grate, with the dry rind of old Cheddar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of' gives E and R, the final letters of 'stale' and 'Cheddar', grated with I SELECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Leicester is an English hard cheese from Leicestershire.

clue.text: Leaders of anarchic gangs get rollicking over such behaviour?

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, so each of the five words gives its first

explanation.surface: Heads of lawless gangs get a telling-off for their conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rollicking' is British slang for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, violent conduct, which anarchic gangs show.

clue.text: Air underwear briefly

definitions.meaning: a rising current of warm air used by gliders and birds
short for the long warm undergarments worn in winter

explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a column of rising warm air, and thermals is the shortened name for warm long underwear.

clue.text: Old Bill on telly making regular appearances? That's right

parts.note: ex means former or old
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: every other letter of telly appears, a regular pattern

explanation.surface: The police on TV turning up every week, which is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' reads as British slang for the police, but splits into old and an account; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly is said to agree with someone, just as that's right is.
